manual_capacity_transcription.basis: Visual full pages and details cross-checked against full braced-staff PDF boundaries. Adjacent double/final lines cluster within3pt for this input only; cross-staff stems excluded. Courtesy key signatures can lie beyond the actual music boundary. Not a general recognizer or full rhythmic collation.

specific_reading_findings.fact: Two-note tremolo and written lower sextuplet paths have distinct tasks; each pair of written minim endpoints spans two quarter beats.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: Logical second endpoint is distinct from visual midpoint. Old native shorter-stroke study referenced, not rerun or applied.

specific_reading_findings.fact: Alternating layer under melody, later single-note tremolo quasi shamisen with grace details, then ordinary long harmony and sparse accompaniment.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: Do not unify ordinary beams, single-note strokes and two-note alternation by blackness or count strokes as a proven playback recipe.

specific_reading_findings.fact: Cross-staff common-beam path plus separate sustained/answering layers.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: Preserve route and conditional independent rests; repeated pitched motion is not automatically a two-note tremolo.

specific_reading_findings.fact: Unslashed whole-note octave at86, single-note3-stroke repeat at87 with poco accel., grace/detail and poco rit. at88; lower staff rests throughout these three bars.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: Holding and restarting repetition differ; no full-player rest or inherited tremolo across the entire ending.

specific_reading_findings.fact: K establishes6/8,dotted-quarter58; local a tempo follows in that context. Later dotted-quarter66,70,74, then R common-time quarter64.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: No automatic reset to J quarter64 or E quarter128; preserve musical unit before comparing numbers.

specific_reading_findings.fact: Local r.h. hand brackets in lower-staff running voice.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: Hand allocation, slur and dynamic are different annotations; no full hand assignment inferred.

specific_reading_findings.fact: 8va continues across O label and ends mid first O bar.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: Do not snap octave endpoints to structural labels or entire phrases; no complete playback/pitch audit.

specific_reading_findings.fact: Upper dotted-quarter rest and lower small leading rest/3-bracket coexist.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: Preserve each layer and include actual group rest; not all rests belong to the same tuplet.

specific_reading_findings.fact: sfz, subsequent mf and later ff have different entries; later two-staff tremolo, receiving long-note connections,lunga and caesura precede R.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: No global dynamic merging or assumed physical/sonic release. Exact end of repetition and following hold semantics remain to be checked in editable source.

specific_reading_findings.fact: Common-time quarter64/pp tail, molto rit., actual2/4 at177 then common time178 and final179.
specific_reading_findings.judgment: Climactic holds do not terminate the score; preserve actual metre and sustained receiving chords.

page_findings.567: Cue must be audible, matching useful rhythm rather than only musical prominence; rhythmic references and instrumental-entry labels have specific jobs.
page_findings.568: Availability of cued performer matters; repeated patterns may fail unique location. Allow preparation/correction time, not only the closest cue.
page_findings.569: Cue scale/spacing distinguishes role; ledger pitch positions remain full-staff based. Content is selective; page-turn cues follow the turn.
page_findings.570: Labelled source, conventional versus outward cue stems and full-bar rest counting are conditional choices.
page_findings.571: Player rests remain full size; crowded ordinary-stem cues can omit them only with enough role contrast; hand-copying differs.
page_findings.572: Playing line has its own rests/accidentals. Open cue ties indicate continued heard notes, not automatic piano resonance or release.
page_findings.573: Short cue generally uses player-clef or indicated octave; longer cue may change clef, but player-clef restored and warned before entry.
page_findings.574: Transposition follows receiving instrument; octave-transposing score conventions remain contextual, not ordinary piano8va rules.
page_findings.575: Extra octave clefs often redundant; cue stave supports simultaneous coordination, independence and some alternatives; its layout continues on576.
